proposals.before: She then gave him in marriage the daughter she had raised—the daughter of Master Ma—who became Empress Xiaoci the Great.
proposals.after: He then gave him in marriage the daughter he had raised—the daughter of Master Ma—who became Empress Xiaoci the Great.
proposals.reason: Chinese 乃妻以 continues with Zixing (or the household head) as subject; literal correctly has He, but idiomatic wrongly makes Lady Zhang the giver of the marriage.

proposals.before: Peng Da said, "As long as I am here, who would dare abuse your father!"
proposals.after: Peng Da said, "As long as I am here, who would dare abuse your father-in-law!"
proposals.reason: 而翁 here is father-in-law: Taizu had married Zixing's foster daughter, so Zixing is his father-in-law; the literal rendering is correct.

proposals.before: During Hongzhi (1488–1505), a Guo Hu claimed his fourth-generation ancestor Laoshi was the prince's fourth son and was granted official rank to conduct sacrifices.
proposals.after: During Hongzhi (1488–1505), a Guo Hu claimed his fourth-generation ancestor Laoshe was the prince's fourth son and was granted official rank to conduct sacrifices.
proposals.reason: 老舍 is rendered Laoshe in s0072 (Guo Laoshe) but inconsistently as Laoshi here.

proposals.before: The Board of Rites ruled: "The Hongwu Emperor established these rites and declared the prince had no heirs; the temple stele is explicit—Laoshi was not his son."
proposals.after: The Board of Rites ruled: "The Hongwu Emperor established these rites and declared the prince had no heirs; the temple stele is explicit—Laoshe was not his son."
proposals.reason: Same 老舍 romanization inconsistency as s0073; should match Guo Laoshe.

decisions.reason: After 子興喜 and Lady Zhang’s speech in s0015, 乃妻以 resumes with Zixing as subject giving the foster daughter in marriage; idiomatic She wrongly makes Lady Zhang the giver, while He matches the Chinese and the literal.
Peng Da answers Taizu’s appeal (s0028); 而翁 addresses him about Zixing, who is his father-in-law after the Ma foster-daughter marriage, so father-in-law is the correct kinship reading.
s0073’s 老舍 is the same name as Guo Laoshe in s0072; Laoshi misromanizes 舍, and Laoshe restores consistent, correct pinyin without other change.
s0075 again names 老舍, already established as Guo Laoshe; Laoshi is the same romanization error and Laoshe is the accurate replacement.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0001 shows the fosterer of 所撫馬公女 is Zixing, the subject of 乃妻以; Lady Zhang as foster parent was created only by the bad She/she raised reading and has no separate support in s0016.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0003 shows English Laoshi came only from the bad romanization of 老舍; the alternate-name claim must read Laoshe while keeping zh, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
